ARABIC LANGUAGE — MOCK EXAM #2
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: ARABIC LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which sentence means 'I have a brother and a sister'? (1 mark)
   A. man haadhihi?
   B. ʿindii akh wa ukht
   C. ummii tatbukhu
   D. haadhaa abii

2. What is imitative speaking? (1 mark)
   A. Listening carefully and copying what you hear
   B. Speaking without a model
   C. Writing from memory
   D. Reading silently

3. How is the Arabic word مَطْبَخٌ read aloud in English letters? (1 mark)
   A. sikkiin
   B. matbakh
   C. ghurfa
   D. milʿaqa

4. How do you say 'on Monday'? (1 mark)
   A. ghadan l-ithnayn
   B. al-yawm ithnayn
   C. yawma l-ithnayn
   D. usbuuʿ l-ithnayn

5. What does the Arabic word اُخْرُجْ (ukhruj) mean? (1 mark)
   A. stand up
   B. raise your hand
   C. open the door
   D. go out

6. Why are special occasions important for a community? (1 mark)
   A. They are only for the rich
   B. They bring people together and help them to live in peace
   C. They are only for children
   D. They make people quarrel

7. What does the Arabic sentence عِيدٌ مُبَارَكٌ mean? (1 mark)
   A. May you be well every year.
   B. Do you have a party? (to a boy)
   C. Happy birthday.
   D. Blessed festival (Happy Eid).

8. How is the Arabic word كَعْكَةٌ read aloud in English letters? (1 mark)
   A. kaʿka
   B. ʿasiir
   C. dawruka
   D. taʿaam

9. Which Arabic sentence means "Do you like bananas?" (1 mark)
   A. هَلْ تُحِبُّ الْمَوْزَ؟
   B. أُحِبُّ الْمَوْزَ
   C. أَشْرَبُ الْمَاءَ
   D. آكُلُ الْخُبْزَ

10. What does the Arabic word ارْفَعْ يَدَكَ (irfaʿ yadaka) mean? (1 mark)
   A. listen
   B. stand up
   C. read
   D. raise your hand

11. What does the Arabic word فَمٌ (fam) mean? (1 mark)
   A. tongue
   B. mouth
   C. hair
   D. face

12. What does the Arabic word ادْخُلْ (udkhul) mean? (1 mark)
   A. come in
   B. open the door
   C. listen
   D. close your eyes

13. Which sound does the Arabic letter ب make? (1 mark)
   A. a quick rolled r
   B. k as in kite
   C. th as in think
   D. b as in bag

14. Which mark gives the short vowel 'a'? (1 mark)
   A. kasra, a small line below the letter
   B. fatHa, a small slanted line above the letter
   C. sukuun, a small circle
   D. Damma, a small curl above the letter

15. How do you read the syllable نَ? (1 mark)
   A. su
   B. na
   C. tu
   D. ta

16. How many syllables are in the word kataba (ka-ta-ba)? (1 mark)
   A. 1
   B. 2
   C. 3
   D. 4

17. Which letter begins the word taawila? (1 mark)
   A. thaa, ث
   B. taa, the light ت
   C. daal, د
   D. Taa, the heavy ط

18. What does the little word li- mean in li-Aminata? (1 mark)
   A. on
   B. for
   C. in
   D. and

19. How is the Arabic word مَوْزٌ read aloud in English letters? (1 mark)
   A. milh
   B. sukkar
   C. mawz
   D. samak

20. Which sound does the Arabic letter ر make? (1 mark)
   A. th as in think
   B. b as in bag
   C. l as in lamp
   D. a quick rolled r

21. How is the Arabic word طَاوِلَةٌ read aloud in English letters? (1 mark)
   A. miftaah
   B. taawila
   C. qalam
   D. sariir

22. What does the Arabic sentence أَنَا أُحِبُّ الْحَفْلَةَ mean? (1 mark)
   A. We dance.
   B. I have a gift.
   C. I like the party.
   D. My mother cooks the food.

23. What does nahnu narqusu mean? (1 mark)
   A. We dance.
   B. My mother cooks.
   C. I have a gift.
   D. I like the party.

24. What is word spacing? (1 mark)
   A. The colour of ink
   B. The small space between words
   C. The number of dots
   D. The height of letters

25. Which Arabic word means "apples"? (1 mark)
   A. رِجْلٌ
   B. تُفَّاحٌ
   C. صَدِيقٌ
   D. جَدَّةٌ

26. Which Arabic word means "leg"? (1 mark)
   A. ظَهْرٌ
   B. سِنٌّ
   C. بَطْنٌ
   D. رِجْلٌ

27. Which Arabic sentence means "My hand is small." (1 mark)
   A. رَأْسِي كَبِيرٌ
   B. أَغْسِلُ وَجْهِي
   C. يَدِي صَغِيرَةٌ
   D. أُنَظِّفُ أَسْنَانِي

28. Which Arabic word means "flower"? (1 mark)
   A. سَحَابٌ
   B. غَائِمٌ
   C. زَهْرَةٌ
   D. مَطَرٌ

29. What does the Arabic sentence أُحِبُّ بَيْتِي mean? (1 mark)
   A. This is my room.
   B. In the room there is a bed.
   C. I like my house.
   D. In the kitchen there is a table.

30. What does it mean if a paragraph is coherent? (1 mark)
   A. It is very long
   B. It is written in colour
   C. Its sentences fit together and make sense
   D. It has only one word

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Translate into English: unadhdhifu asnaanii (2 marks)

32. Spell the word باب by naming the letters in order, and give its meaning. (3 marks) (3 marks)

33. Explain how the weather affects our daily life. Give two examples. (3 marks) (3 marks)

34. Explain why it is important to know the days of the week. (2 marks) (2 marks)

35. State the job of each part of a speech: opening, middle and closing. (3 marks) (3 marks)

36. Translate into English: al-qalamu fii l-haqiiba (2 marks)

37. Write two describing words in Arabic sounds with their meanings, one for a masculine and one for a feminine item. (3 marks) (3 marks)

38. Name two common foods in your area and write one Arabic sentence about one of them, with its meaning. (3 marks) (3 marks)

39. Give three rules for a handwriting contest. (3 marks) (3 marks)

40. Translate into English: asmaʿu bi-udhunii (2 marks)

41. Give three ways of taking care of your body. (3 marks) (3 marks)

42. Write three body parts in Arabic sounds with meanings. (3 marks) (3 marks)

43. Translate into English: al-jawwu ghaa'im (2 marks)

44. Write four parts of the body in Arabic sounds with meanings. (4 marks) (4 marks)

45. Translate into English: yadii Sagiira (2 marks)

46. Translate into English: anaa bi-khayr, al-hamdu lillaah (2 marks)

47. Explain how to build a vocabulary bank for the theme of the body. (3 marks) (3 marks)

48. Translate into English: ʿalaa t-taawilati kaʿka (2 marks)

49. Give three rules for taking turns in a conversation. (3 marks) (3 marks)
pages.answers:
ARABIC LANGUAGE — MOCK EXAM #2 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — ʿindii akh wa ukht
   ʿindii means 'I have', akh is brother, wa is 'and' and ukht is sister.

2. A — Listening carefully and copying what you hear
   In imitative speaking we listen to a speaker and copy the sounds, speed and tone.

3. B — matbakh
   مَطْبَخٌ is read matbakh and means kitchen.

4. C — yawma l-ithnayn
   yawma l-ithnayn means 'on the day of Monday'.

5. D — go out
   اُخْرُجْ (ukhruj) means go out.

6. B — They bring people together and help them to live in peace
   Celebrations bring families and friends together and build unity.

7. D — Blessed festival (Happy Eid).
   عِيدٌ مُبَارَكٌ (ʿiid mubaarak) means: Blessed festival (Happy Eid).

8. A — kaʿka
   كَعْكَةٌ is read kaʿka and means cake.

9. A — هَلْ تُحِبُّ الْمَوْزَ؟
   هَلْ تُحِبُّ الْمَوْزَ؟ (hal tuhibbu l-mawz?) means: Do you like bananas?

10. D — raise your hand
   ارْفَعْ يَدَكَ (irfaʿ yadaka) means raise your hand.

11. B — mouth
   فَمٌ (fam) means mouth.

12. A — come in
   ادْخُلْ (udkhul) means come in.

13. D — b as in bag
   The letter ب makes the sound b as in bag.

14. B — fatHa, a small slanted line above the letter
   fatHa is the mark for the short vowel a.

15. B — na
   نَ is read na.

16. C — 3
   ka + ta + ba makes three syllables.

17. D — Taa, the heavy ط
   طَاوِلَةٌ begins with the heavy letter Taa.

18. B — for
   li- means 'for', so li-Aminata is 'for Amina'.

19. C — mawz
   مَوْزٌ is read mawz and means bananas.

20. D — a quick rolled r
   The letter ر makes the sound a quick rolled r.

21. B — taawila
   طَاوِلَةٌ is read taawila and means table.

22. C — I like the party.
   أَنَا أُحِبُّ الْحَفْلَةَ (anaa uhibbu l-hafla) means: I like the party.

23. A — We dance.
   nahnu means we and narqusu means we dance.

24. B — The small space between words
   Word spacing is the neat gap between one word and the next.

25. B — تُفَّاحٌ
   تُفَّاحٌ (tuffaah) means apples.

26. D — رِجْلٌ
   رِجْلٌ (rijl) means leg.

27. C — يَدِي صَغِيرَةٌ
   يَدِي صَغِيرَةٌ (yadii Sagiira) means: My hand is small.

28. C — زَهْرَةٌ
   زَهْرَةٌ (zahra) means flower.

29. C — I like my house.
   أُحِبُّ بَيْتِي (uhibbu baytii) means: I like my house.

30. C — Its sentences fit together and make sense
   A coherent paragraph has related sentences in a sensible order.

SECTION B
----
31. (2 marks)
   Answer: I clean my teeth.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

32. (3 marks)
   Answer: baa, alif, baa. It means door.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the letters, 1 mark for the order and 1 mark for the meaning.

33. (3 marks)
   Answer: Rain helps crops to grow; hot sun makes us look for shade; we choose our clothes by the weather.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the idea and 1 mark for each example.

34. (2 marks)
   Answer: Days help us to plan what to do and to use time well, for example school, homework and rest.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for planning and 1 mark for good use of time.

35. (3 marks)
   Answer: Opening: greet and say who you are. Middle: give the information. Closing: thank the audience.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each part.

36. (2 marks)
   Answer: The pen is in the bag.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

37. (3 marks)
   Answer: kabiir (big) for a masculine word and kabiira (big) for a feminine word.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each form and 1 mark for the meaning.

38. (3 marks)
   Answer: For example maize and bananas. al-mawzu ladhiidh. The banana is delicious.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for two foods, 1 mark for a correct sentence and 1 mark for its meaning.

39. (3 marks)
   Answer: Everyone writes the same words for the same time; judges look at shape, size, spacing and neatness; everyone is encouraged and praised.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each sensible rule.

40. (2 marks)
   Answer: I hear with my ear.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

41. (3 marks)
   Answer: Wash hands and face; clean teeth; eat good food; sleep well; play outdoors.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid way.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: For example raʾs (head), yad (hand), fam (mouth).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct word with meaning.

43. (2 marks)
   Answer: The weather is cloudy.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

44. (4 marks)
   Answer: For example raʾs (head), ʿayn (eye), fam (mouth), yad (hand).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct word with meaning.

45. (2 marks)
   Answer: My hand is small.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

46. (2 marks)
   Answer: I am well, thanks be to God.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

47. (3 marks)
   Answer: Write each new word with its sound and meaning, add a small drawing, and keep the words on cards or a page for practice.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid step.

48. (2 marks)
   Answer: On the table there is a cake.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

49. (3 marks)
   Answer: Listen until the speaker finishes; do not speak at the same time; use polite words to interrupt; give others a chance.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid rule.
